section_summary: This section contains company claims and State Department correspondence about patents, royalties, shares, and other property interests in postwar Japan. Its central document is a proposed U.S. policy on Japanese patents, covering restoration of Allied rights, licensing, publication of wartime inventions, and Japanese patent rights abroad. Later letters ask about filing new applications and protecting existing patents.

subfiles.title: International General Electric statement of Japanese property interests, concluding page
subfiles.from: Arthur T. Brown, International General Electric Company
subfiles.about: Lists the company's Japanese financial claims and requests that U.S. authorities in Japan receive the figures.
subfiles.summary: Lists Japanese government notes, Mitsui deposits, a Tokyo office fund, a Tokyo-Shibaura advance, and office equipment.

subfiles.title: Reply to J. A. H. Torry on company property interests
subfiles.about: Reports discussion of a plan for American companies to help investigate and protect their property in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Martin acknowledges the company's letters and says a property investigation plan is under discussion.

subfiles.title: Request for reports on International General Electric interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Arthur T. Brown, International General Electric Company
subfiles.about: Requests reports on Tokyo-Shibaura, company shares, licensed patents, and debts.
subfiles.summary: Brown seeks information about Tokyo-Shibaura's condition, wartime share sales and proceeds, patents due for assignment under a prewar license, and outstanding financial claims.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about filing U.S. patent applications in Japan
subfiles.about: Asks whether Americans can obtain Japanese patents and whom to contact for filing clearance.
subfiles.summary: The company asks about reopening patent applications in Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to American Chemical Paint Company
subfiles.about: States that Japanese patent filing procedures have not been reestablished.
subfiles.summary: Boskey promises a public announcement when filing resumes.

subfiles.title: Transmission of International General Electric correspondence
subfiles.about: Sends copies of an October letter and related requests concerning company interests in Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Torry supplies Martin with correspondence previously sent to Gantenbein.

subfiles.title: Request for action on International General Electric letters
subfiles.about: Asks Gantenbein to act on enclosed property valuations and information requests.
subfiles.summary: Torry describes two enclosed letters about Tokyo-Shibaura shares, obligations, and requested reports.

subfiles.title: Reply on Walter Kidde royalty claim
subfiles.about: Advises that Walter Kidde's claim against Mitsui is a private debt normally pursued through ordinary remedies.
subfiles.summary: English says the Department cannot yet assess possible changes through peace negotiations and encloses a release on eased communications restrictions.

subfiles.title: Walter Kidde claim against Mitsui Bussan Kaisha
subfiles.from: A. M. Doxsey, Walter Kidde & Company
subfiles.about: Submits a royalty reimbursement claim against Mitsui with an earlier explanatory letter.
subfiles.summary: Doxsey asks the Department to accept the claim and acknowledge it.

subfiles.title: Manufacturing license arrangement for Kidde products in Japan
subfiles.from: A. M. Doxsey, Walter Kidde & Company
subfiles.about: Details a prewar Mitsui manufacturing license and unpaid royalties for fire protection equipment.
subfiles.summary: Doxsey describes the 1933 exclusive license, equipment covered, and royalty terms. He says payments ceased after October 1940, estimates annual royalties of $7,500–$10,000, and requests investigation and collection.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Walter Kidde royalty claim
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Mitsui royalty claim and refers it to the Legal Adviser.
subfiles.summary: Martin directs further inquiries to the Legal Adviser's office.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding proposed Japanese patent policy
subfiles.about: Submits a draft U.S. position on Japanese domestic and foreign patents for committee review.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring recommends referral to the Far East subcommittee.

subfiles.title: Treatment of Japanese domestic and foreign patents
subfiles.to: State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee; proposed submission to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Proposes policy for patents in Japan and Japanese-owned patent rights abroad.
subfiles.summary: The paper reviews occupation directives, Japanese patent law, Allied property restoration, German patent policy, reparations, and economic deconcentration. Its proposed policy would restore eligible Allied patent rights, regulate royalties and licensing, end secret patents, publish wartime technical material, and open Japanese-owned foreign patents for general use. It also proposes controlled foreign patent applications for peaceful Japanese inventions made after 1945.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting Parker Pen correspondence
subfiles.to: Mr. McDiarmid, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Forwards Parker Pen correspondence and a possible reply about Japanese patents.
subfiles.summary: Vernon suggests McDiarmid's office may send the revised reply.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Parker Pen Company
subfiles.about: Addresses Parker Pen's concern that Japanese fountain pens imitate its protected designs.
subfiles.summary: The draft notes SCAP's assurances, suggests supplying patent and manufacturer details for investigation, and explains that correspondence with Japan is currently limited to exchanging information.

subfiles.title: Reply on Northern Equipment Company claims
subfiles.about: Reports a request for an expedited Tokyo report and asks when patent taxes were last paid.
subfiles.summary: Flaherty promises to relay information received from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Northern Equipment follow-up on Japanese claims
subfiles.about: Requests an update on claims previously raised in September 1946.
subfiles.summary: The company asks whether further information is available.

subfiles.title: Airgram requesting Northern Equipment report
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests an expedited report on Northern Equipment Company's interests.
subfiles.summary: The airgram cites earlier Department despatches and asks for prompt reporting.

subfiles.title: Parker Pen comments on Japanese imitation pens
subfiles.from: Ivan D. Tefft, Parker Pen Company
subfiles.about: Argues that a Japanese pen copies Parker's Vacumatic design and urges stronger patent protection for foreigners.
subfiles.summary: Tefft says prewar Japanese patents gave foreign makers weak protection and that imitation pens caused market confusion. He offers infringement records and suggests working with the Japanese Patent Office during the occupation.

subfiles.title: Northern Equipment request for claims guidance
subfiles.about: Seeks a claims update and instructions for filing against assets held by the Alien Property Custodian.
subfiles.summary: The company cites a possible June 1 filing deadline.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on patenting a fish processing machine in Japan
subfiles.from: Edward R. Taylor, Shorett, Taylor & Revelle
subfiles.about: Asks how inventor E. M. Borg can obtain Japanese patent rights for a fish processing machine.
subfiles.summary: Taylor says Japanese fishing interests may use Borg's process.

subfiles.title: Reply on E. M. Borg's Japanese patent inquiry
subfiles.about: States that Japanese patent application procedures have not yet reopened.
subfiles.summary: Rubin says their restoration will be publicized.
